one_liner: Stripe has a broad REST API with self-serve free account API keys (HTTP Basic or bearer) and sandboxes. OAuth for Apps/Connect and the official hosted MCP server are likely but not confirmed by the fetched pages.
auth_notes: Confirmed by the pages: API keys (sk_/rk_) sent as the HTTP Basic username, or as a bearer token. The pages say partner integrations use Stripe Connect to access other Stripe accounts, and Stripe Apps go through app review to be listed. They don't describe the OAuth 2.0 flow itself. OAUTH2 as the multi-user primary rests on Composio's catalog (OAUTH2 managed) and is low confidence. Restricted API keys are a fallback for multi-user access.
access_notes: A free Stripe account gives dashboard-managed API keys. Test mode secret keys (sk_test_) work in sandboxes with no payment. Live mode uses restricted keys (rk_live_) or sk_live_. Listing a public app in the Stripe App Marketplace requires app review, but pasting keys does not.
blocker_notes: Users can paste restricted API keys today. App Marketplace listing needs app review but is not required to ship. None of the fetched pages mention MCP, so the official MCP status rests on the MCP Registry entry com.stripe/mcp. That entry is a hint, not page evidence.
